title: AArch64 page table entry (descriptor)
summary: An AArch64 (ARM 64-bit) page table descriptor is 8 bytes (64 bits). Block descriptor (for large pages): bits 0 = valid, bit 1 = table/block (0=block), bits 2-4 = attribute index, bit 5 = non-secure, bit 6 = access permission (AP), bit 7 = shareability, bit 8 = access flag (AF), bit 9 = not global (nG), bit 10 = reserved, bits 11 = contiguous, bits 12-47 = output address (OA), bits 48-50 = reserved, bit 51 = PXN (privileged execute never), bit 52 = XN (execute never), bits 53-54 = reserved, bits 55-58 = software use, bits 59-60 = reserved, bit 61 = DBM (dirty bit modifier), bit 62 = contiguous, bit 63 = software use. Table descriptor: bit 0 = valid, bit 1 = table, bits 2-47 = next level table address.

Block descriptor (for large pages): bits 0 = valid, bit 1 = table/block (0=block), bits 2-4 = attribute index, bit 5 = non-secure, bit 6 = access permission (AP), bit 7 = shareability, bit 8 = access flag (AF), bit 9 = not global (nG), bit 10 = reserved, bits 11 = contiguous, bits 12-47 = output address (OA), bits 48-50 = reserved, bit 51 = PXN (privileged execute never), bit 52 = XN (execute never), bits 53-54 = reserved, bits 55-58 = software use, bits 59-60 = reserved, bit 61 = DBM (dirty bit modifier), bit 62 = contiguous, bit 63 = software use. Table descriptor: bit 0 = valid, bit 1 = table, bits 2-47 = next level table address.

structure.meaning: 0 = block descriptor (leaf), 1 = table descriptor (points to next level).
Index into MAIR (Memory Attribute Indirection Register).
00 = non-shareable, 01 = reserved, 10 = outer shareable, 11 = inner shareable.
Set by hardware on access. Used for page replacement.
1 = not global (ASID-tagged, flushed on context switch).
Physical address of the block/table (aligned to page size).
Hint that this entry is contiguous with the next (for TLB optimization).
Dirty Bit Modifier: hardware sets the dirty bit (AP[1]) on write instead of raising a fault.

notes: AArch64 uses 4-level paging (L0 -> L1 -> L2 -> L3) by default, or 3-level with 64KB pages.
Page sizes: 4KB (L3), 2MB (L2 block), 1GB (L1 block), 512MB (L1 block with 64KB granule).
TTBR0 (user) and TTBR1 (kernel) hold the base addresses of the page tables.
ASID (Address Space ID) tags TLB entries to avoid flushes on context switch.
ARM uses MAIR for memory attribute indirection (cache policy, shareability).
